subject.title: fix(copilot): bound BYOK proxy request bodies

question: Should OpenClaw impose one universal 16 MiB aggregate body cap and 30-second total-read deadline on every Copilot BYOK provider request?
rationale: The existing Copilot provider path defines no such universal envelope, and selecting these values determines which previously accepted provider requests fail after upgrade.

options.title: Calibrate a conservative envelope
options.body: Choose limits and timeout semantics from representative text, tool, multimodal, and slow-upload Copilot requests, then update focused proof.

options.title: Accept 16 MiB and 30 seconds
options.body: Intentionally own the proposed rejection boundary after proving representative supported workloads fit inside it.

options.title: Pause fixed limits
options.body: Keep the PR open until upstream guidance or measured workload evidence supports a safe universal policy.

recommendation.title: Calibrate a conservative envelope
recommendation.body: Choose limits and timeout semantics from representative text, tool, multimodal, and slow-upload Copilot requests, then update focused proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the Copilot BYOK proxy and are the strongest feature-history owner for its supported request contract.
